  history reference or built-in genome rather than a default branch.

  objects. Use legacy format onl

    with zipfile.ZipFile(path) as z:

            root=ET.fromstring(z.read('xl/sharedStrings.xml'))
            for si in root.findall('a:si',ns):
                texts=[]
                for t in si.findall('.//a:t',ns): texts.append(t.text or '')
                shared.append(''.join(texts))
        wb=ET.fromstring(z.read('xl/workbook.xml'))
        rels=ET.fromstring(z.read('xl/_rels/workbook.xml.rels'))
        rid_to_target={rel.attrib['Id']: rel.attrib['Target'] for rel in rels}
        for sh in wb.findall('a:sheets/a:sheet',ns):
            name=sh.attrib['name']; rid=sh.attrib['{http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/officeDocument/2006/relationships}id']
            target='xl/'+rid_to_target[rid].lstrip('/')
            print('\\nSHEET',name,'TARGET',target)
            root=ET.fromstring(z.read(target))
            for row in root.findall('.//a:sheetData/a:row',ns)[:maxrows]:
                vals=[]
                for c in row.findall('a:c',ns):
                    typ=c.attrib.get('t'); v=c.find('a:v',ns)
                    if v is None: vals.append(''); continue
                    text=v.text or ''
                    if typ=='s': text=shared[int(text)]
                    vals.append(text)

Use this skill for UDT execution mechanics. It does not prescribe what a UDT
should compute or how its outputs should be interpreted.

3. Author a clear `GalaxyUserTool` representation for the intended program.

## Minimal UDT

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis
version: 0.1.0
container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |
  set -eu
  application-command \
    --input "$(inputs.input.path)" \
    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:
  - name: result
    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, time, os
ann=pd.read_csv('GSE255742_Amphioxus_21hpf_sc_annotations.tsv.gz',sep='\\t')
# define mapping options
base_map={
'endoderm':['endoderm'],
'endostyle_csg':['endostyle_csg'],
'epidermal_neural':['epidermal_neural1','epidermal_neural2'],
'epidermis':['epidermis_1','epidermis_2'],
'mesodermal_notochord':['mesodermal_notochord'],
'muscular_somites':['muscular_somites'],
'neural':['neural'],
'neural_like':['neural_like1','neural_like2'],
'putative_neuro_endo':['putative_neuro_endo'],
'somite':['somite'],
'tailbud':['tailbud'],
'tailbud_neural':['tailbud_neural'],
}
# add alternative neural incl DiMes HyTh for later as neural_plus
map2=dict(base_map); map2['neural_plus']=['neural','DiMes','HyTh']
# cells in ann only
cell_to_type=ann.set_index('cell')['cell_type'].to_dict()
# read header for cells
import gzip
with gzip.open('GSE255742_Amphioxus_21hpf_sc_UMI_counts.tsv.gz','rt') as f:
    header=f.readline().rstrip('\\n').split('\\t')
print('n cells header',len(header),'ann',len(cell_to_type))
# group indices (columns in data excluding index start at pandas cols)
groups={k:set(v) for k,v in map2.items()}
# make vector group label per cell for all map groups, for separate cell_types duplicated OK? Each cell assigned one group except neural_plus overlaps neural.
# For base agg only
base_cols=list(base_map.keys())
agg=None
idx_all=[]
start=time.time()
for ci,chunk in enumerate(pd.read_csv('GSE255742_Amphioxus_21hpf_sc_UMI_counts.tsv.gz',sep='\\t',index_col=0,chunksize=1000,compression='gzip')):
    # initialize output with row index
    out=pd.DataFrame(index=chunk.index)
    # sum per group by selecting columns whose cell_type in list; could precompute col lists once
    if ci==0:
        col_lists={g:[c for c in chunk.columns if cell_to_type.get(c) in types] for g,types in base_map.items()}
        col_lists['neural_plus']=[c for c in chunk.columns if cell_to_type.get(c) in map2['neural_plus']]
        print({g:len(v) for g,v in col_lists.items()})
    for g,cols in col_lists.items():
        out[g]=chunk[cols].sum(axis=1)
    if agg is None:
        agg=out
    else:
        agg=pd.concat([agg,out])
    if ci%5==0: print('chunk',ci,'rows',agg.shape[0],'elapsed',round(time.time()-start,1), flush=True)
print('done',agg.shape,'time',time.time()-start)
# normalize CPM for each group
cpm=agg.div(agg.sum(axis=0),axis=1)*1e6
cpm.to_csv('public_pseudobulk_cpm.tsv.gz',sep='\\t',compression='gzip')
print('sums',agg.sum())
# compare to local
local=pd.read_csv('sample.swap.rna.q1.tsv.gz',sep='\\t',index_col=0,compression='gzip')
common=local.index.intersection(cpm.index)
print('common',len(common),'local rows',local.shape[0],'cpm rows',cpm.shape[0])
# correlations local x public base (incl neural_plus)
cor=pd.DataFrame(index=local.columns,columns=cpm.columns,dtype=float)
for lc in local.columns:
    for pc in cpm.columns:
        cor.loc[lc,pc]=np.corrcoef(local.loc[common,lc],cpm.loc[common,pc])[0,1]
print(cor.round(6).to_string())
# also max absolute diff after matching names
for name in local.columns:
    pc='neural_plus' if name=='neural' else name
    if pc in cpm:
        diff=(local[name]-cpm.loc[local.index,pc]).abs()
        print('diff',name,pc,'max',diff.max(),'mean',diff.mean(),'corr',cor.loc[name,pc])
PY"

import gzip, csv, sys, time, math
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
ann=pd.read_csv('GSE255742_Amphioxus_21hpf_sc_annotations.tsv.gz',sep='\\t')
cols_sample=[]
with gzip.open('sample.swap.rna.q1.tsv.gz','rt') as f:
    cols_sample=f.readline().rstrip('\\n').split('\\t')[1:]
print('sample columns', cols_sample)

def collapse(ct):
    if ct.startswith('epidermal_neural'):
        return 'epidermal_neural'
    if ct.startswith('epidermis_'):
        return 'epidermis'
    if ct.startswith('neural_like'):
        return 'neural_like'
    if ct in cols_sample:
        return ct
    return None
ann['grp']=ann['cell_type'].map(collapse)
print('group cell counts')
print(ann.groupby('grp')['cell'].count().reindex(cols_sample).to_string())
cell_to_grp=dict(zip(ann['cell'],ann['grp']))
ng=len(cols_sample); grp_index={g:i for i,g in enumerate(cols_sample)}
# Read UMI table and aggregate by group for all rows
out_genes=[]; sums=[]; totals=np.zeros(ng,dtype=np.float64)
with gzip.open('GSE255742_Amphioxus_21hpf_sc_UMI_counts.tsv.gz','rt') as f:
    header=f.readline().rstrip('\\n').split('\\t')
    idx=np.array([grp_index[cell_to_grp.get(c)] if cell_to_grp.get(c) in grp_index else -1 for c in header], dtype=np.int16)
    keep=idx>=0
    idx_keep=idx[keep]
    print('cells in groups', keep.sum(), 'of', len(header), flush=True)
    for n,line in enumerate(f,1):
        parts=line.rstrip('\\n').split('\\t')
        gene=parts[0]
        vals=np.fromiter((int(x) for x in parts[1:]), dtype=np.int32, count=len(header))
        bc=np.bincount(idx_keep, weights=vals[keep], minlength=ng).astype(np.float64)
        out_genes.append(gene); sums.append(bc); totals += bc
        if n % 5000 == 0:
            print('processed', n, flush=True)
mat=np.vstack(sums)
print('genes', mat.shape, 'totals', dict(zip(cols_sample, totals)))
cpm=mat/totals*1e6
# read suspect
sus_genes=[]; sus=[]
with gzip.open('sample.swap.rna.q1.tsv.gz','rt') as f:
    header=f.readline().rstrip('\\n').split('\\t')[1:]
    for line in f:
        p=line.rstrip('\\n').split('\\t')
        sus_genes.append(p[0]); sus.append([float(x) for x in p[1:]])
sus=np.array(sus); print('sus', sus.shape)
# gene order comparison
print('gene order equal', out_genes==sus_genes)
# restrict common
pos={g:i for i,g in enumerate(out_genes)}
idx2=[pos[g] for g in sus_genes if g in pos]
idxs=[i for i,g in enumerate(sus_genes) if g in pos]
ref=cpm[idx2,:]
sus2=sus[idxs,:]
# correlations and max abs diffs by pair
print('\\nmax abs diff reference group -> suspect col')
diff=np.zeros((ng,ng))
for i,g in enumerate(cols_sample):
    for j,h in enumerate(header):
        diff[i,j]=np.max(np.abs(ref[:,i]-sus2[:,j]))
print('header', header)
for i,g in enumerate(cols_sample):
    best=diff[i].argmin()
    print(g, 'best', header[best], 'diff', diff[i,best], 'diag', diff[i,i])
# Pearson log1p corr ref vs suspect
A=np.log1p(ref); B=np.log1p(sus2)
A=(A-A.mean(0))/A.std(0); B=(B-B.mean(0))/B.std(0)
corr=A.T@B/(A.shape[0]-1)
print('\\ncorrelation reference group rows -> suspect cols')
print('       '+' '.join([h[:8].ljust(10) for h in header]))
for i,g in enumerate(cols_sample):
    row=' '.join([f'{corr[i,j]:.4f}'.ljust(10) for j in range(ng)])
    best=corr[i].argmax()
    print(g.ljust(22), row, 'best', header[best])
PY"

representation.description: Pairwise log-expression correlations and per-column specific genes
representation.shell_command:
python - "$(inputs.matrix.path)" results.tsv <<'PY'

import csv, math, sys
path=sys.argv[1]
out=sys.argv[2]
with open(path, newline="") as fh:
    rd=csv.reader(fh, delimiter="\t")
    header=next(rd)
    names=header[1:]
    cols=[[] for _ in names]
    rawcols=[[] for _ in names]
    genes=[]
    for row in rd:
        if len(row)<len(names)+1: continue
        try: vals=[float(x) for x in row[1:len(names)+1]]
        except: continue
        genes.append(row[0])
        for j,x in enumerate(vals):
            rawcols[j].append(x)
            cols[j].append(math.log1p(x))
def pearson(a,b):
    n=len(a); ma=sum(a)/n; mb=sum(b)/n
    va=sum((x-ma)**2 for x in a); vb=sum((x-mb)**2 for x in b)
    return sum((x-ma)*(y-mb) for x,y in zip(a,b))/math.sqrt(va*vb) if va and vb else 0.0
def ranks(a):
    order=sorted(range(len(a)), key=lambda i:a[i])
    r=[0.0]*len(a); k=0
    while k<len(order):
        l=k+1
        while l<len(order) and a[order[l]]==a[order[k]]: l+=1
        rv=(k+l-1)/2.0
        for z in range(k,l): r[order[z]]=rv
        k=l
    return r
rcols=[ranks(x) for x in cols]
with open(out,"w",newline="") as fo:
    w=csv.writer(fo,delimiter="\t",lineterminator="\n")
    w.writerow(["section","sample1","sample2","value","detail"])
    for i in range(len(names)):
        for j in range(i+1,len(names)):
            w.writerow(["pearson_log1p",names[i],names[j],f"{pearson(cols[i],cols[j]):.8f}",""])
            w.writerow(["spearman_log1p",names[i],names[j],f"{pearson(rcols[i],rcols[j]):.8f}",""])
    for i,nm in enumerate(names):
        vals=[(pearson(cols[i],cols[j]),names[j]) for j in range(len(names)) if j!=i]
        vals.sort(reverse=True)
        w.writerow(["nearest_pearson",nm,vals[0][1],f"{vals[0][0]:.8f}",",".join(f"{b}:{a:.4f}" for a,b in vals[:5])])
        svals=[(pearson(rcols[i],rcols[j]),names[j]) for j in range(len(names)) if j!=i]
        svals.sort(reverse=True)
        w.writerow(["nearest_spearman",nm,svals[0][1],f"{svals[0][0]:.8f}",",".join(f"{b}:{a:.4f}" for a,b in svals[:5])])
    for i,nm in enumerate(names):
        scores=[]
        for g in range(len(genes)):
            x=rawcols[i][g]
            others=[rawcols[j][g] for j in range(len(names)) if j!=i]
            mo=sum(others)/len(others)
            mx=max(others)
            spec=math.log2((x+0.1)/(mo+0.1))
            scores.append((spec,x/(mx+0.1),x,genes[g]))
        scores.sort(reverse=True)
        for rank,(spec,ratio,x,gene) in enumerate(scores[:40],1):
            w.writerow(["specific_gene",nm,gene,f"{spec:.8f}",f"rank={rank};expr={x:.6g};vsmax={ratio:.6g}"])

representation.name: Inspect BLAG annotation overlap
representation.shell_command:
python - "$(inputs.matrix.path)" "$(inputs.gff.path)" overlap.tsv <<'PY'

import csv,re,sys
matrix,gff,out=sys.argv[1:4]
with open(matrix,newline="") as f:
    r=csv.reader(f,delimiter="\t"); next(r)
    genes={row[0] for row in r if row}
hits={}
seen_ids=set()
with open(gff,errors="replace") as f:
    for line in f:
        if not line or line[0]=="#": continue
        p=line.rstrip("\n").split("\t")
        if len(p)<9: continue
        attr=p[8]
        ids=set(re.findall(r"BLAG[0-9A-Za-z_.-]+",attr))
        for x in ids:
            x=x.split(":")[-1]
            seen_ids.add(x)
            if x in genes:
                hits.setdefault(x,set()).add(attr)
with open(out,"w") as f:
    f.write("metric\tvalue\tdetail\n")
    f.write("matrix_gene_count\t%d\t\n"%len(genes))
    f.write("gff_BLAG_id_count\t%d\t\n"%len(seen_ids))
    f.write("intersection_count\t%d\t\n"%len(hits))
    for g in sorted(hits)[:500]:
        f.write("match\t%s\t%s\n"%(g," | ".join(sorted(hits[g]))))

events.command:
python - "/jetstream2/scratch/main/jobs/79036206/inputs/dataset_385004ed-55ab-4e45-b6ba-d027e4e3a891.dat" results.tsv <<'PY'

import csv, math, sys
path=sys.argv[1]
out=sys.argv[2]
with open(path, newline="") as fh:
    rd=csv.reader(fh, delimiter="\t")
    header=next(rd)
    names=header[1:]
    cols=[[] for _ in names]
    rawcols=[[] for _ in names]
    genes=[]
    for row in rd:
        if len(row)<len(names)+1: continue
        try: vals=[float(x) for x in row[1:len(names)+1]]
        except: continue
        genes.append(row[0])
        for j,x in enumerate(vals):
            rawcols[j].append(x)
            cols[j].append(math.log1p(x))
def pearson(a,b):
    n=len(a); ma=sum(a)/n; mb=sum(b)/n
    va=sum((x-ma)**2 for x in a); vb=sum((x-mb)**2 for x in b)
    return sum((x-ma)*(y-mb) for x,y in zip(a,b))/math.sqrt(va*vb) if va and vb else 0.0
def ranks(a):
    order=sorted(range(len(a)), key=lambda i:a[i])
    r=[0.0]*len(a); k=0
    while k<len(order):
        l=k+1
        while l<len(order) and a[order[l]]==a[order[k]]: l+=1
        rv=(k+l-1)/2.0
        for z in range(k,l): r[order[z]]=rv
        k=l
    return r
rcols=[ranks(x) for x in cols]
with open(out,"w",newline="") as fo:
    w=csv.writer(fo,delimiter="\t",lineterminator="\n")
    w.writerow(["section","sample1","sample2","value","detail"])
    for i in range(len(names)):
        for j in range(i+1,len(names)):
            w.writerow(["pearson_log1p",names[i],names[j],f"{pearson(cols[i],cols[j]):.8f}",""])
            w.writerow(["spearman_log1p",names[i],names[j],f"{pearson(rcols[i],rcols[j]):.8f}",""])
    for i,nm in enumerate(names):
        vals=[(pearson(cols[i],cols[j]),names[j]) for j in range(len(names)) if j!=i]
        vals.sort(reverse=True)
        w.writerow(["nearest_pearson",nm,vals[0][1],f"{vals[0][0]:.8f}",",".join(f"{b}:{a:.4f}" for a,b in vals[:5])])
        svals=[(pearson(rcols[i],rcols[j]),names[j]) for j in range(len(names)) if j!=i]
        svals.sort(reverse=True)
        w.writerow(["nearest_spearman",nm,svals[0][1],f"{svals[0][0]:.8f}",",".join(f"{b}:{a:.4f}" for a,b in svals[:5])])
    for i,nm in enumerate(names):
        scores=[]
        for g in range(len(genes)):
            x=rawcols[i][g]
            others=[rawcols[j][g] for j in range(len(names)) if j!=i]
            mo=sum(others)/len(others)
            mx=max(others)
            spec=math.log2((x+0.1)/(mo+0.1))
            scores.append((spec,x/(mx+0.1),x,genes[g]))
        scores.sort(reverse=True)
        for rank,(spec,ratio,x,gene) in enumerate(scores[:40],1):
            w.writerow(["specific_gene",nm,gene,f"{spec:.8f}",f"rank={rank};expr={x:.6g};vsmax={ratio:.6g}"])

# Galaxy UDT Authoring

Use this skill for UDT execution mechanics. It does not prescribe what a UDT
should compute or how its outputs should be interpreted.

## Workflow

1. Map the program or command to its Galaxy inputs, output files, runtime, and
   resource needs.
2. Find and verify a live pinned runtime that contains the required
   implementation.
3. Author a clear `GalaxyUserTool` representation for the intended program.
   Combine stages only when no intermediate result can change, reject, or
   invalidate a downstream stage. Otherwise run the diagnostic or prerequisite
   first, or make the command stop before do

# Galaxy Tool Submission

Use this skill after the scientific tool and parameters have been selected. Build
complex inputs from the selected wrapper's live schema and verify the created job
resolved the intended objects.

## Dataset Inputs

- Wait for uploaded data to reach `ok` with the expected datatype before using
  the final history dataset ID.
- Verify paired mates use distinct dataset IDs and preserve forward/reverse
  order.
- For reference-source conditionals, confirm the job resolved the intended
  history reference or built-in genome rather than a default branch.

## Large Public Or Reference Objects

- Stage an authoritative public or refere

# Galaxy UDT Implementation Reference

Read only the section needed for the current implementation or failure.

- [Minimal UDT](#minimal-udt)
- [Staged generated script](#staged-generated-script)
- [Short base64 fallback](#short-base64-fallback)
- [Resource fields](#resource-fields)
- [Execution failures](#execution-failures)

The YAML blocks are authoring examples. The API representation may be serialized
as JSON.

## Minimal UDT

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis
version: 0.1.0
container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |
  set -eu
  application-command \
    --input "$(inputs.input.path)" \
    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:
  - name: result
    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

# Use previous data compute total diagonal spearman for all swaps
import pandas as pd,numpy as np,gzip
from scipy.stats import spearmanr
ann=pd.read_csv('/workspace/GSE255742_annotations.tsv',sep='\\t'); meta_ct=ann.groupby('metacell')['cell_type'].agg(lambda s:s.value_counts().idxmax()).to_dict(); meta_n=ann.groupby('metacell').size().to_dict()
true=pd.read_csv('/workspace/GSE255742_metacell_expr.tsv',sep='\\t',index_col=0,low_memory=False); true.columns=[int(c) for c in true.columns]
sub={}
for c in true.columns: sub.setdefault(meta_ct[c],[]).append(c)
tc=pd.DataFrame(index=true.index)
for ct,cols in sub.items():
 w=np.array([meta_n[c] for c in cols],float); tc[ct]=np.average(true[cols].values,axis=1,weights=w)
merges={'endoderm':['endoderm'],'endostyle_csg':['endostyle_csg'],'epidermal_neural':['epidermal_neural1','epidermal_neural2'],'epidermis':['epidermis_1','epidermis_2'],'mesodermal_notochord':['mesodermal_notochord'],'muscular_somites':['muscular_somites'],'neural':['neural'],'neural_like':['neural_like1','neural_like2'],'putative_neuro_endo':['putative_neuro_endo'],'somite':['somite'],'tailbud':['tailbud'],'tailbud_neural':['tailbud_neural']}
tm=pd.DataFrame(index=tc.index)
for ct,subs in merges.items():
 w=np.array([ann[ann.cell_type==s].shape[0] for s in subs],float); tm[ct]=(tc[subs].values@w)/w.sum()
tm=tm/tm.sum()*1e6
hdr=None;ids=[];vals=[]
with gzip.open('/workspace/inputs/sample.swap.rna.q1.tsv.gz','rt') as f:
 hdr=f.readline().rstrip('\\n').split('\\t')[1:]
 for line in f:
  p=line.rstrip('\\n').split('\\t'); ids.append(p[0]); vals.append(list(map(float,p[1:])))
M=pd.DataFrame(vals,index=ids,columns=hdr)
common=[g for g in tm.index if g in M.index]; A=tm.loc[common].values; B=M.loc[common].values
corr=np.zeros((len(hdr),len(hdr)))
for i in range(len(hdr)):
 for j in range(len(hdr)):
  corr[i,j]=spearmanr(B[:,i],A[:,j])[0]
base=sum(corr[k,k] for k in range(len(hdr)))
print('base',base)
pairs=[]
for i in range(len(hdr)):
 for j in range(i+1,len(hdr)):
  # swapped labels => input i now assigned true j, input j true i
  score=base - corr[i,i]-corr[j,j] + corr[i,j]+corr[j,i]
  pairs.append((score-base,i,j,score,hdr[i],hdr[j]))
pairs.sort(reverse=True)
for d,i,j,score,a,b in pairs[:15]:
 print(f'{d:+.4f} {a},{b} score={score:.4f} cross={corr[i,j]:.3f},{corr[j,i]:.3f} self={corr[i,i]:.3f},{corr[j,j]:.3f}')

order=['endoderm','endostyle_csg','epidermal_neural','epidermis','mesodermal_notochord','muscular_somites','neural','neural_like','putative_neuro_endo','somite','tailbud','tailbud_neural']
# rows 0-11 ref, 12-23 query
# delta for pair i,j = D[i,i+12]+D[j,j+12]-D[i,j+12]-D[j,i+12]
pairs=[]
for i in range(12):
 for j in range(i+1,12):
  delta=float(D[i,i+12]+D[j,j+12]-D[i,j+12]-D[j,i+12])
  pairs.append((delta,i,j,D[i,i+12],D[j,j+12],D[i,j+12],D[j,i+12]))
pairs_sorted=sorted(pairs,key=lambda x:(-x[0],order[x[1]],order[x[2]]))
for p in pairs_sorted[:10]:
 delta,i,j,di,dj,cij,cji=p
 print(f'{order[i]},{order[j]} delta={delta:.6f} self={di:.6f},{dj:.6f} cross={cij:.6f},{cji:.6f}')
best=pairs_sorted[0]
margin=best[0]-pairs_sorted[1][0]

# correlation = 1-D best diagonal/cross

for i in range(12):

should compute or how its outputs should be interpreted.

## Workflow

1. Map the program or command to its Galaxy inputs, output files, runtime, and
   resource needs.
2. Find and verify a live pinned runtime that contains the required
   implementation.
3. Author a clear `GalaxyUserTool` representation for the intended program.
   Combine stages only when no intermediate result can change, reject, or
   invalidate a downstream stage. Otherwise run the diagnostic or prerequisite
   first, or make the command stop before do

The YAML blocks are authoring examples. The API representation may be serialized
as JSON.

## Minimal UDT

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis
version: 0.1.0
container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |
  set -eu
  application-command \
    --input "$(inputs.input.path)" \
    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:
  - name: result
    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

/bin/bash -lc "cat > /workspace/analysis_compare.py <<'PY'
#"'!/usr/bin/env python3
import gzip
import math
import os
import sys

def open_maybe(path, mode='"'rt'):
    if path.endswith('.gz'):
        return gzip.open(path, mode)
    # sniff gzip magic
    with open(path, 'rb') as f:
        magic = f.read(2)
    if magic == b'\\x1f\\x8b':
        return gzip.open(path, mode)
    return open(path, mode)

def read_supplied(path):
    # returns ordered gene list, ordered labels, dict gene->row vector
    genes = []
    labels = None
    rows = []
    with open_maybe(path) as f:
        for line_no, line in enumerate(f):
            if not line.strip():
                continue
            parts = line.rstrip('\\n').split('\\t')
            if line_no == 0:
                labels = parts[1:]
                continue
            genes.append(parts[0])
            rows.append([float(x) for x in parts[1:]])
    return genes, labels, rows

def read_annotation(path):
    # returns cell -> group (merged supplied-level)
    cell_to_group = {}
    with open_maybe(path) as f:
        header = None
        for line in f:
            if not line.strip():
                continue
            parts = line.rstrip('\\n').split('\\t')
            if header is None:
                header = parts
                continue
            cell = parts[0]
            ct = parts[1]
            cell_to_group[cell] = ct
    return cell_to_group

GROUP_MAP = {
    'endoderm': 'endoderm',
    'endostyle_csg': 'endostyle_csg',
    'epidermal_neural1': 'epidermal_neural',
    'epidermal_neural2': 'epidermal_neural',
    'epidermis_1': 'epidermis',
    'epidermis_2': 'epidermis',
    'mesodermal_notochord': 'mesodermal_notochord',
    'muscular_somites': 'muscular_somites',
    'neural': 'neural',
    'neural_like1': 'neural_like',
    'neural_like2': 'neural_like',
    'putative_neuro_endo': 'putative_neuro_endo',
    'somite': 'somite',
    'tailbud': 'tailbud',
    'tailbud_neural': 'tailbud_neural',
}

def main():
    supplied_path = sys.argv[1]
    counts_path = sys.argv[2]
    ann_path = sys.argv[3]
    ref_out = sys.argv[4]
    comp_out = sys.argv[5]

    genes, labels, supplied = read_supplied(supplied_path)
    n_genes = len(genes)
    n_lab = len(labels)
    gene_index = {g: i for i, g in enumerate(genes)}

    cell_to_group = read_annotation(ann_path)
    # map fine cell type to merged group, exclude non-mapped
    label_to_group = {lbl: lbl for lbl in labels}
    group_labels = list(labels)

    # Build column group assignment from raw counts header
    group_to_cols = {g: [] for g in group_labels}
    ignored_cells = 0
    unknown_cells = 0
    cell_count_by_group = {g: 0 for g in group_labels}
    with open_maybe(counts_path) as f:
        header = f.readline().rstrip('\\n').split('\\t')
        # first col is gene id
        cell_columns = header[1:]
        col_group = [None] * len(cell_columns)
        for j, cell in enumerate(cell_columns):
            ct = cell_to_group.get(cell)
            if ct is None:
                unknown_cells += 1
                continue
            grp = GROUP_MAP.get(ct)
            if grp is None:
                ignored_cells += 1
                continue
            col_group[j] = grp
            group_to_cols[grp].append(j)
            cell_count_by_group[grp] += 1

    # accumulate raw sums for supplied genes only
    sums = [[0.0] * n_lab for _ in range(n_genes)]
    total_per_group = [0.0] * n_lab
    processed = 0
    with open_maybe(counts_path) as f:
        f.readline()
        for line in f:
            if not line.strip():
                continue
            parts = line.rstrip('\\n').split('\\t')
            g = parts[0]
            gi = gene_index.get(g)
            if gi is None:
                continue
            vals = parts[1:]
            row_sums = [0.0] * n_lab
            for j, valstr in enumerate(vals):
                grp = col_group[j]
                if grp is None:
                    continue
                if valstr == '0' or valstr == '':
                    continue
                v = float(valstr)
                gi_group = label_to_group[grp]
                row_sums[gi_group] += v
            for gi_group, v in enumerate(row_sums):
                if v:
                    sums[gi][gi_group] += v
            processed += 1

    for k in range(n_lab):
        total_per_group[k] = sum(sums[i][k] for i in range(n_genes))
    cpm = [[(sums[i][k] / total_per_group[k] * 1e6) if total_per_group[k] > 0 else 0.0 for k in range(n_lab)] for i in range(n_genes)]

    with open(ref_out, 'w') as out:
        out.write('gene\\t' + '\\t'.join(group_labels) + '\\n')
        for i, g in enumerate(genes):
            out.write(g + '\\t' + '\\t'.join(f'{cpm[i][k]:.10g}' for k in range(n_lab)) + '\\n')

    # Pearson correlations between supplied columns and reference groups
    supplied_by_col = [[supplied[i][k] for i in range(n_genes)] for k in range(n_lab)]
    ref_by_group = [[cpm[i][k] for i in range(n_genes)] for k in range(n_lab)]
    with open(comp_out, 'w') as out:
        out.write('supplied_label\\t' + '\\t'.join(group_labels) + '\\tbest_match\\tbest_corr\\tself_corr\\tself_rank\\n')
        for a, lab in enumerate(labels):
            x = supplied_by_col[a]
            corrs = []
            for b in range(n_lab):
                y = ref_by_group[b]
                corrs.append(pearson(x, y))
            best_i = max(range(n_lab), key=lambda i: corrs[i])
            self_i = a
            ranked = sorted(range(n_lab), key=lambda i: -corrs[i])
            self_rank = ranked.index(self_i) + 1
            out.write(lab + '\\t' + '\\t'.join(f'{c:.9f}' for c in corrs) + '\\t' + group_labels[best_i] + '\\t' + f'{corrs[best_i]:.9f}' + '\\t' + f'{corrs[self_i]:.9f}' + '\\t' + str(self_rank) + '\\n')

    # also write per-column diagnostics to stderr? no, stdout summary
    print('processed_genes', processed, 'n_supplied_genes', n_genes)
    print('cell_counts_by_group', cell_count_by_group)
    print('total_per_group', total_per_group)

def pearson(x, y):
    n = len(x)
    if n == 0:
        return float('nan')
    mx = sum(x) / n
    my = sum(y) / n
    sxy = sum((a - mx) * (b - my) for a, b in zip(x, y))
    sxx = sum((a - mx) ** 2 for a in x)
    syy = sum((b - my) ** 2 for b in y)
    if sxx == 0 or syy == 0:
        return float('nan')
    return sxy / math.sqrt(sxx * syy)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()
PY

import zipfile, re, gzip, csv, collections
# extract mapping gene_id note ID -> gene symbol and locus_tag from GTF gene and transcript lines
z=zipfile.ZipFile('[REDACTED LOCAL PATH]')
map_id={}
with z.open('ncbi_dataset/data/GCA_927797965.1/genomic.gtf') as f:
    for line in f:
        if line.startswith(b'#'): continue
        s=line.decode(errors='replace').rstrip('\\n')
        parts=s.split('\\t')
        if len(parts)<9: continue
        attrs=parts[8]
        # note field has ID:BLAG...;~source...
        m=re.search(r'ID:(BLAG\\d+)_\\d+', attrs)
        if not m: continue
        bid=m.group(1)
        gm=re.search(r'gene \"(["'^"]+)"'"',attrs)
        locus=re.search(r'locus_tag \"(["'^"]+)"'"',attrs)
        # prefer gene-level line (gbkey Gene) if multiple; transcript line has transcript too but gene same
        if bid not in map_id or 'Gene' in attrs:
            map_id[bid]=(gm.group(1) if gm else '', locus.group(1) if locus else '')
print('mapping count', len(map_id))
# load matrix gene ids
p='inputs/sample.swap.rna.q1.tsv.gz'
with gzip.open(p,'rt') as f:
    r=csv.reader(f,delimiter='\\t'); header=next(r)
    genes=[]; mat=[]
    for row in r:
        genes.append(row[0]); mat.append([float(x) for x in row[1:]])
print('genes',len(genes),'mapped',sum(g in map_id for g in genes))
# print some mapping for first ids and missing
for g in genes[:20]:
    print(g, map_id.get(g))
# Save mapping table
with open('[REDACTED LOCAL PATH]','w') as f:
    for g in genes:
        sym,loc=map_id.get(g,('',''))
        f.write(f'{g}\\t{sym}\\t{loc}\\n')
PY"

# read UMI once per line streaming, sum counts per group

# Actually need initialize zeros lazily; we'll read first header to map cell->col groups
with gzip.open('[REDACTED LOCAL PATH]','rt') as f:
    r=csv.reader(f,delimiter='\\t'); header=next(r)
    cell_to_col={c:i for i,c in enumerate(header)}
    group_cols={g:[cell_to_col[c] for c in cell_to_col if ann.get(c) in types] for g,types in groups.items()}
    print('cells per group', {g:len(v) for g,v in group_cols.items()})
    total={g:0 for g in groups}

    for row in r:
        gid=row[0]

        for h,v in zip(header,vals): cols[h][g]=v
# read ref
ref={}
with open('[REDACTED LOCAL PATH]') as f:
    r=csv.reader(f,delimiter='\\t'); hh=next(r)[1:]
    colsr={h:{} for h in hh}
    for row in r:
        g=row[0]; vals=list(map(float,row[1:]))
        for h,v in zip(hh,vals): colsr[h][g]=v
inhead=header
rhead=hh
print('input header',inhead)
print('ref header',rhead)
# correlations spearman and pearson between input and ref columns
import scipy.stats as st
for i,hi in enumerate(inhead):
    best=[]
    for hr in rhead:
        xs=[cols[hi][g] for g in cols[hi]]
        ys=[colsr[hr].get(g,0) for g in cols[hi]]
        # skip? pearson log
        rp=st.pearsonr(xs,ys)[0]
        rs=st.spearmanr(xs,ys)[0]
        best.append((rp,rs,hr))

# Galaxy UDT Authoring

Use this skill for UDT execution mechanics. It does not prescribe what a UDT
should compute or how its outputs should be interpreted.

## Workflow

1. Map the program or command to its Galaxy inputs, output files, runtime, and
   resource needs.
2. Find and verify a live pinned runtime that contains the required
   implementation.
3. Author a clear `GalaxyUserTool` representation for the intended program.
   Combine stages only when no intermediate result can change, reject, or
   invalidate a downstream stage. Otherwise run the diagnostic or prerequisite
   first, or make the command stop before do

Read only the section needed for the current implementation or failure.

- [Minimal UDT](#minimal-udt)
- [Staged generated script](#staged-generated-script)

The YAML blocks are authoring examples. The API representation may be serialized
as JSON.

## Minimal UDT

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis
version: 0.1.0
container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |
  set -eu
  application-command \
    --input "$(inputs.input.path)" \
    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:
  - name: result
    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

# Examples

These are optional implementation examples, not required steps for every UDT.

## RDS And S4 Inspection

Use the validated image below when a UDT needs R, S4, or sparse `Matrix`
support:

```text
quay.io/chiujunhao24/udt:rds-sparse-r4.5.3-matrix1.7.5-r1
```

Stage `scripts/inspect_rds.R` as a typed script input. First produce a bounded
JSON structure report without choosing a metadata member:

```sh
Rscript "$(inputs.script.path)" \
  "$(inputs.input.path)" \
  rds_report.json \
  metadata.tsv
```

Inspect `rds_report.json`. If it identifies a tabular member needed by the
analysis, run the script again with that exact member name:

```sh
Rscript "$(inputs.script.path)" \
  "$(inputs.input.path)" \
  rds_report.json \
  metadata.tsv \
  meta.data
```

Declare both outputs with `from_work_dir`. The first run records that metadata
extraction was not request

# get our IDs
our=[]

    import gzip
    with gzip.open(raw) as g:

def fetch_range(start,end):
    req=urllib.request.Request(baseurl, headers={'Range':f'bytes={start}-{end}'})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=300) as r:
        return r.read()

print('local_len',local_len,'compressed',f['cs'])

out=os.path.join(os.getcwd(), name)
start=f['off']+local_len; end=f['off']+local_len+f['cs']-1
print('downloading',end-start+1,'bytes')
with open(out,'wb') as w:
    pos=start
    chunk=10_000_000
    while pos<=end:
        e=min(pos+chunk-1,end)
        data=fetch_range(pos,e)
        if not data:
            print('empty at',pos); break
        w.write(data)
        pos=e+1

# decompress raw deflate

/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, re
g=pd.read_csv('gene_pseudobulk.tsv',sep='\\t',index_col=0)
cols=g.columns.tolist()
log=np.log1p(g)
# marker sets, gene names in matrix (uppercase or regex)
marker_sets={
'endoderm':['FOXA2','FOXA1','HHEX','GATA4','GATA5','GATA6','NKX2-2','PDX1','CDX4','SOX17','HNF4A'],
'endostyle_csg':['NKX2-1','FOXE1','PAX9','SIX1','EYA4','TBX1','FOXQ1','TPO','RSPO2','FOXL1'],
'epidermal_neural':['DLX1','PAX2','ZIC1','WNT3','HOXB6','TMPRSS5','SIX3','SOX2','FOXQ2'],
'epidermis':['KRT13','KRT75','KRT84','FOXJ1','TP63','SHH','DSP','COL17A1','SPINT1'],
'mesodermal_notochord':['T','FOXA2','COL1A2','SHH','CHRD','SOX9','NOG','TGFB2','PTPRQ','LOXL1'],
'muscular_somites':['MYOD1','MYF5','MYL1','ACTC1','MYH7','CKM','MEOX2','NEXN','MYLK','TNNI2'],
'neural':['ELAVL4','SOX2','TUBB2B','NEUROD4','CHAT','SLC32A1','OLIG3','CELF3','NCAM1','PRDM8'],
'neural_like':['ASCL1','PRDM12','POU4F3','NTRK2','SYT2','LHFPL4','SHH','ELAVL4','SOX14','POU4F3'],
'putative_neuro_endo':['PAX2','CDX4','HOXB6','EVX1','OLIG3','TBX6','TBX16','SOX2','WNT3','MSGN1'],
'somite':['ALX4','TCF21','PODN','FOXF1','WNT5A','NEUROD4','FOXG1','EN2','FERD3L','RIPPLY2'],
'tailbud':['WNT1','FGF17','T','OTP','EMX2','ZSCAN22','MAP3K10','EVX2','CDX1','CDX4'],
'tailbud_neural':['ELAVL4','SOX2','PAX2','CDX4','HOXB6','WNT3','EVX2','ZIC1','NEUROD4','TUBB2B'],
}
# For each set, score each column as mean of z-scored or log expression; use robust scaled log per gene across columns then mean
scores=pd.DataFrame(index=marker_sets.keys(), columns=cols)
for ct, ms in marker_sets.items():
    # find genes present, choose exact case-insensitive; for slash etc handle later
    genes=[]
    for m in ms:
        hits=[x for x in g.index if x.upper()==m.upper()]
        if not hits:
            pat=re.compile('"'^'"'+re.escape(m), re.I)
            hits=[x for x in g.index if pat.search(x)]
        genes += hits[:2]
    genes=list(dict.fromkeys(genes))
    print('\\n',ct,'genes',len(genes),genes[:20])
    if not genes: continue
    sub=log.loc[genes]
    # zscore each gene across columns
    z=sub.sub(sub.mean(axis=1),axis=0).div(sub.std(axis=1)+1e-9,axis=0)
    # mean zscore (negative genes hurt)
    scores.loc[ct]=z.mean(axis=0)
print('\\nScores (rows true labels, cols predicted)')
print(scores.round(2).to_string())
print('\\nBest predicted per column')
for c in cols:
    print(c, scores[c].idxmax(), scores[c].max().round(2))
print('\\nFor each label, best column')
for ct in marker_sets:
    print(ct, scores.loc[ct].idxmax(), scores.loc[ct].max().round(2))
PY"

/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, gzip, time
print('loading counts...')
t=time.time()
counts=pd.read_csv('[REDACTED LOCAL PATH]',sep='\\t',index_col=0)
print('loaded',counts.shape,'time',time.time()-t)
# annot
ann=pd.read_csv('[REDACTED LOCAL PATH]',sep='\\t',index_col=0)
# merge cell types: normalize names to our 12
rename={'epidermis_1':'epidermis','epidermis_2':'epidermis','epidermal_neural1':'epidermal_neural','epidermal_neural2':'epidermal_neural','neural_like1':'neural_like','neural_like2':'neural_like'}
ann['ct']=ann['cell_type'].map(rename).fillna(ann['cell_type'])
print(ann.ct.value_counts())
# subset counts columns to cells with our ct (exclude HyTh/DiMes)
cts=set(['endoderm','endostyle_csg','epidermal_neural','epidermis','mesodermal_notochord','muscular_somites','neural','neural_like','putative_neuro_endo','somite','tailbud','tailbud_neural'])
cells=ann[ann.ct.isin(cts)].index
print('cells kept',len(cells),'of',len(ann))
common_cols=counts.columns.intersection(cells)
print('common cols',len(common_cols))
# subset and aggregate sum by ct
sub=counts.loc[:,common_cols]
print('sub shape',sub.shape)
ct=ann.loc[common_cols,'ct']
agg=sub.groupby(ct,axis=1).sum()
print('agg shape',agg.shape)
# normalize each column to sum 1e6 (like our file)
cpm=agg.div(agg.sum(axis=0),axis=1)*1e6
# subset genes to ours
ours=pd.read_csv('sample.swap.rna.q1.tsv.gz',sep='\\t',index_col=0)
common_genes=ours.index.intersection(cpm.index)
print('genes common',len(common_genes))
ref=cpm.loc[common_genes]
our=ours.loc[common_genes]
print('ref columns',ref.columns.tolist())
# save
ref.to_csv('ref_pseudobulk_cpm.tsv',sep='\\t')
our.to_csv('our_subset.tsv',sep='\\t')
print('done')
PY"

/bin/bash -lc "python3 - <<'PY'
import pandas as pd, numpy as np
ref=pd.read_csv('ref_pseudobulk_cpm.tsv',sep='\\t',index_col=0)
our=pd.read_csv('our_subset.tsv',sep='\\t',index_col=0)
print(ref.shape,our.shape)
print('col sums ref',ref.sum().round(0).tolist())
print('col sums our',our.sum().round(0).tolist())
# Pearson log1p
X=np.log1p(ref); Y=np.log1p(our)
corr=pd.DataFrame(np.corrcoef(Y.T, X.T)[:12,12:], index=our.columns, columns=ref.columns)
# actually corrcoef block order [our 12, ref 12], block [12:24, 0:12]
corr=pd.DataFrame(np.corrcoef(Y.T, X.T)[12:24, :12], index=our.columns, columns=ref.columns)
print('\\nPearson log1p corr (our rows x ref cols)')
print(corr.round(4).to_string())
# spearman maybe
from scipy.stats import spearmanr
print('\\nBest ref for each our col (Pearson)')
for c in our.columns:
    r=corr.loc[c]
    print(c,'->',r.idxmax(),r.max().round(4),'diag',corr.loc[c,c].round(4))
print('\\nBest our for each ref col')
for c in ref.columns:
    r=corr[c]
    print(c,'->',r.idxmax(),r.max().round(4),'diag',corr.loc[c,c].round(4))
# rank correlations maybe
print('\\nSpearman correlation selected')
for c in our.columns:

import pandas as pd, numpy as np
p='sample.swap.rna.q1.tsv.gz'
df=pd.read_csv(p,sep='\\t',index_col=0)
# cpm-like; compute log2((mean in group+1e-5)/(mean other+1e-5))
cols=df.columns
# scale each column? sums approx equal; use raw
for col in cols:
    a=df[col].values
    b=(df.drop(columns=col).sum(axis=1)).values
    # total per group mean with same total? compare rates: a/sumA, b/sumB
    rate_a=a/df[col].sum(); rate_b=b/df.drop(columns=col).values.sum()
    lfc=np.log2((rate_a+1e-6)/(rate_b+1e-6))
    idx=np.argsort(-lfc)[:25]
    print('\\n###',col)
    for i in idx:
        print(df.index[i], 'lfc=%.2f'%lfc[i], 'val=%.1f'%a[i], 'other=%.3f'%(b[i]/ (len(cols)-1)))
PY"

/bin/bash -lc "cat > parse_gbff.py <<'PY'
import re, json, sys
path='ref3/ncbi_dataset/data/GCA_927797965.1/genomic.gbff'
out='gbff_id_gene.json'
pat_id=re.compile(r'\\bID:(BLAG\\d+)(?:[_;]|"'$)'"')
pat_gene=re.compile(r'/gene=\"(["'^"]+)"'"')
pat_locus=re.compile(r'/locus_tag=\"(["'^"]+)"'"')
mapping={}
current_gene=None
current_locus=None
count=0
with open(path, 'r', errors='ignore') as f:
    for line in f:
        stripped=line.strip()
        m=pat_gene.search(stripped)
        if m:
            current_gene=m.group(1)
        m=pat_locus.search(stripped)
        if m:
            current_locus=m.group(1)
        # A new feature? current gene persists; if ID line then map
        for m in pat_id.finditer(stripped):
            gid=m.group(1)
            if gid not in mapping:
                mapping[gid]={'gene':current_gene,'locus':current_locus}
                count+=1
            elif current_gene and mapping[gid]['gene'] is None:
                mapping[gid]['gene']=current_gene
                mapping[gid]['locus']=current_locus
print('mapped',count,'ids')
json.dump(mapping, open(out,'w'))
print('saved',out)
PY

# map our labels to original cell_type patterns
patterns={
 'endoderm':['endoderm'],
 'endostyle_csg':['endostyle_csg'],
 'epidermal_neural':['epidermal_neural1','epidermal_neural2'],
 'epidermis':['epidermis_1','epidermis_2'],
 'mesodermal_notochord':['mesodermal_notochord'],

 'neural':['neural'],

 'putative_neuro_endo':['putative_neuro_endo'],
 'somite':['somite'],
 'tailbud':['tailbud'],
 'tailbud_neural':['tailbud_neural'],
}
ann['group']=ann['cell_type'].map(lambda x: next((k for k,vals in patterns.items() if x in vals), None))
print(ann['group'].value_counts(dropna=False))

# Load our genes
our=pd.read_csv('sample.swap.rna.q1.tsv.gz',sep='\\t',index_col=0)
our_genes=set(our.index)
print('our genes',len(our_genes))

# Open sc_counts, process rows
path='ref/sc_counts.tsv.gz'
fin=gzip.open(path,'rt')
header=fin.readline().rstrip('\\n').split('\\t')
# map cell->group
cell_group={}
for cell,g in zip(ann['cell'],ann['group']):
    cell_group[cell]=g
# Some cells in header not annotations? check
missing=[c for c in header if c not in cell_group]
print('header cells',len(header),'missing annotations',len(missing),missing[:5])
groups=list(patterns.keys())
group_sums={g:np.zeros(len(header),dtype=np.float64) for g in groups}
# We'll accumulate directly using mapping array
gidx=np.array([groups.index(cell_group.get(c)) if cell_group.get(c) in groups else -1 for c in header], dtype=np.int32)
counts_per_group=np.bincount(gidx[gidx>=0], minlength=len(groups))

kept=[]

3. Author a clear `GalaxyUserTool` representation for the intended program.

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis
version: 0.1.0
container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |
  set -eu
  application-command \
    --input "$(inputs.input.path)" \
    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:
  - name: result
    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

# User-Defined Tools (Beta)

Starting with Galaxy 25.0, users can create their own tools without requiring administrator privileges to install them. These tools are written in YAML, defined through the Galaxy user interface, and stored in the database.

## Differences from Standard Galaxy Tools

Standard Galaxy tools are written in XML and have broad access to the Galaxy database and filesystem during the command and configuration file templating phase, which uses the Cheetah templating language.

For example, the following XML tool command section queries the Galaxy database and writes a file to the home directory of the system user running the Galaxy process:

```xml
    #from pathlib import Path
    #user_id = $__app__.model.session().query($__app__.model.User.id).one()
    #open(f"{Path.home()}/a_file", "w").write("Hello!")
]]></command>
```

Feature-wise Correlation Tests
==============================

Galaxy wrapper for per-feature correlations between matched tabular matrices.

The tool aligns observations by an identifier column, aligns features by column
name for matrices with headers, computes one Pearson or Spearman correlation
test per feature, drops missing values within each feature pair, applies
Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and reports both a per-feature table and a
summary table.

This is useful when two assays are measured across the same samples or models
and the scientific question is one test per matched feature.

import json
import urllib.request
history_id = 'bbd44e69cb8906b5a35709fd765e28c2'
input_id = 'f9cad7b01a4721351ca88276438f1fc3'
blocks = [(2,21),(22,121),(122,321)]
blocks += [(322,1321 + 1000*i) for i in range(21)]
blocks += [(21322,21452)]
# Keep the fixed non-overlapping layout explicit and remove any accidental duplicate.
seen = set()
blocks = [b for b in blocks if not (b in seen or seen.add(b))]
galaxy_key = open('[REDACTED LOCAL PATH]').read().strip()
results = []
for start, end in blocks:
    inputs = {'input1': {'src': 'hda', 'id': input_id}, 'groupcol': '1', 'ignorecase': False}
    for i, col in enumerate(range(start, end + 1)):
        inputs[f'operations_{i}|optype'] = 'mean'
        inputs[f'operations_{i}|opcol'] = str(col)
        inputs[f'operations_{i}|opround'] = 'no'
        inputs[f'operations_{i}|opdefault'] = '0'
    payload = {'tool_id': 'Grouping1', 'history_id': history_id, 'inputs': inputs}
    req = urllib.request.Request('https://usegalaxy.org/api/tools', data=json.dumps(payload).encode(), headers={'x-api-key': galaxy_key, 'content-type': 'application/json'}, method='POST')
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req) as resp:
        data = json.load(resp)
    results.append({'start':start, 'end':end, 'job':data['jobs'][0]['id'], 'output':data['outputs'][0]['id']})
print(json.dumps(results))

# Galaxy UDT Authoring

Use this skill for UDT execution mechanics. It does not prescribe what a UDT
should compute or how its outputs should be interpreted.

## Workflow

1. Map the program or command to its Galaxy inputs, output files, runtime, and
   resource needs.
2. Find and verify a live pinned runtime that contains the required
   implementation.
3. Author a clear `GalaxyUserTool` representation for the intended program.
   Combine stages only when no intermediate result can change, reject, or
   invalidate a downstream stage. Otherwise run the diagnostic or prerequisite

# Galaxy UDT Implementation Reference

Read only the section needed for the current implementation or failure.

- [Minimal UDT](#minimal-udt)
- [Staged generated script](#staged-generated-script)
- [Short base64 fallback](#short-base64-fallback)
- [Resource fields](#resource-fields)
- [Execution failures](#execution-failures)

The YAML blocks are authoring examples. The API representation may be serialized
as JSON.

## Minimal UDT

Replace the container placeholder with a verified pinned tag. Use a bare tagged
reference without `docker://` or a digest.

```yaml
class: GalaxyUserTool
id: analysis-v1
name: Analysis
version: 0.1.0
container: quay.io/biocontainers/<package>:<pinned-tag>

shell_command: |
  set -eu
  application-command \
    --input "$(inputs.input.path)" \
    --output result.tsv

inputs:
  - name: input
    type: data
    format: [tabular]

outputs:
  - name: result
    type: data
    format: tabular
    from_work_dir: result.tsv
```

# User-Defined Tools (Beta)

Starting with Galaxy 25.0, users can create their own tools without requiring administrator privileges to install them. These tools are written in YAML, defined through the Galaxy user interface, and stored in the database.

## Differences from Standard Galaxy Tools

Standard Galaxy tools are written in XML and have broad access to the Galaxy database and filesystem during the command and configuration file templating phase, which uses the Cheetah templating language.

For example, the following XML tool command section queries the Galaxy database and writes a file to the home directory of the system user running the Galaxy process:

```xml
    #from pathlib import Path
    #user_id = $__app__.model.session().query($__app__.model.User.id).one()
    #open(f"{Path.home()}/a_file", "w").write("Hello!")
]]></command>
```

import pandas as pd, numpy as np, time
# load metadata and challenge matrix

ctmap=dict(zip(ann.cell,ann.grp))
# read header to establish cell order; small read
head=pd.read_csv('GSE255742_counts.tsv.gz',sep='\\t',nrows=0)
cells=head.columns.tolist()
groups=np.array([ctmap.get(c,'') for c in cells])
print('cells',len(cells),'desired',[(g,int((groups==g).sum())) for g in wanted])

    a=ch.to_numpy(dtype=np.float64,copy=False)
    vals=np.column_stack([a[:,groups==g].sum(axis=1) for g in wanted])
    out.append(vals); nrows+=len(ch)
    if (k+1)%10==0: print('chunk',k+1,'rows',nrows,'sec',round(time.time()-t,1),flush=True)
agg=np.vstack(out); genes=pd.concat([ch.index for ch in []]) if False else None
# Need indexes: rerun? collected index in loop
# Oops preserve index separately above; handled below via new processing not possible; use row order and read all index cheaply
idx=pd.read_csv('GSE255742_counts.tsv.gz',sep='\\t',usecols=[0],skiprows=1,header=None,names=['gene'])['gene'].to_numpy()
print('agg shape',agg.shape,'idx',len(idx),'time',time.time()-t)
# normalize CPM (raw source)
sums=agg.sum(axis=0); cpm=agg/sums*1e6

# compare challenge to ref correlations, and all permutations best assignment

 best=cor.argmax(axis=1)
 print('best',[(wanted[i],wanted[j],round(cor[i,j],3)) for i,j in enumerate(best)])
 # best one-to-one assignment
 from scipy.optimize import linear_sum_assignment
 ri,cj=linear_sum_assignment(-cor)
 print('assign',[(wanted[i],wanted[j],round(cor[i,j],3)) for i,j in zip(ri,cj)],'sum',cor[ri,cj].sum())

import pandas as pd, gzip, numpy as np
D=pd.read_csv('sample.swap.rna.q1.tsv.gz',sep='\\t',index_col=0)

am=A[['metacell','cell_type']].drop_duplicates()

# reference average per cell type over metacell columns
# use means by annotation mapping, not cells (unique metacell likely)
mt={r.metacell:r.cell_type for r in am.itertuples()}
refs={}
for ct in sorted(set(mt.values())):
 ids=[str(i) for i,v in mt.items() if v==ct]
 refs[ct]=M[[i for i in ids if i in M.columns]].mean(axis=1)
R=pd.DataFrame(refs)

for dc in D.columns:

print(C.round(3).to_string())
print('best')
for c in D.columns:
 print(c, C.loc[c].nlargest(4).round(3).to_dict())

D=pd.read_csv('sample.swap.rna.q1.tsv.gz',sep='\\t',index_col=0)

# exact annotation cell order is the UMI column order
labels=A.cell_type.to_numpy()
uniq=pd.unique(labels)
li={x:i for i,x in enumerate(uniq)}
g=np.array([li[x] for x in labels],dtype=np.int16)
keep=set(D.index)
out=np.zeros((len(keep),len(uniq)),dtype=np.float64)
rowids=[]
tot=np.zeros(len(uniq),dtype=np.float64)
start=time.time(); n=0; j=0
with gzip.open('umi.tsv.gz','rt') as f:
    f.readline()
    for line in f:
        n+=1
        parts=line.rstrip('\\n').split('\\t')
        gene=parts[0]
        vals=np.fromstring('\\t'.join(parts[1:]),sep='\\t')
        sums=np.bincount(g,weights=vals,minlength=len(uniq))
        tot += sums
        if gene in keep:
            rowids.append(gene)
            out[j,:]=sums
            j+=1
        if n%5000==0: print('rows',n,'kept',j,'sec',round(time.time()-start,1),flush=True)
print('done',n,j,'sec',round(time.time()-start,1),flush=True)
# preserve D order
R=pd.DataFrame(out[:j,:],index=rowids,columns=uniq)
R=R.reindex(D.index)

for a in D.columns:
 for b in uniq:
  C.loc[a,b]=L[a].corr(LR[b])

print('corr')

 print(a,'corr',C.loc[a].nlargest(5).round(4).to_dict(),'mae',MAE.loc[a].nsmallest(5).round(1).to_dict())
